implementation_notes: Kotlin has no try-with-resources statement; the standard library supplies use as an inline extension on Closeable and AutoCloseable, which runs the block with the receiver and then closes it down correctly whether an exception is thrown or not - closing in a compiled finally, adding a close failure to the suppressed exceptions of a failing block and rethrowing it when the block succeeded. The classic owner class is replaced by implement Closeable/AutoCloseable plus call use, so the failure reporting matches Java's try-with-resources without the statement; use returns the block's value and a nullable receiver is not closed. For shared or pooled resources (connections handed out by a pool, streams someone else still writes) closing through use is wrong by construction and the checkout/release API has to be used instead.
code_sketch:
File("app.log").bufferedWriter().use { w ->
    w.write("started\n")
    w.flush()          // surface the errors you care about here
}                      // close() runs on every exit path
pitfalls: use closes only its own receiver: a second resource opened inside the block needs its own use, otherwise an exception between its acquisition and the end of the block leaks it.
Teardown errors are easy to drop: when the block throws, the close failure is only attached as a suppressed exception, so flush/commit explicitly before the block ends when the data matters.
Calling use on a borrowed or cached object (a pooled connection, a singleton stream, a writer shared with another component) closes a resource someone else still owns.
